englishSourceNotes: treat: Danish has no neutral word covering cake + lollipop + popsicle + waffle. 'slik' = candy only; 'dessert' excludes lollipop/popsicle. Chose 'guf' (warm everyday child/parent word for sweet treats). Fallback if judged too colloquial: 'Mit yndlingsslik'.
bug: the row has snail, spider, worm, so NOT 'insekt'. 'smådyr' is the exact børnehave term (smådyrsjagt) and covers all nine pictures.
sea: 'havdyr' is a real, short Danish word; 'Mit yndlingsdyr i havet' would be 23 chars.

vehicle: the row includes airplane, rocket, sailboat, submarine, which are strictly not 'køretøjer' (things that drive). No short Danish word covers land, sea, air and space; 'køretøj' is what children's material uses and the pictures carry it.
farm: 'husdyr' in Danish means farm animals/livestock (pets = kæledyr), so it fits the pattern at 18 chars. 'Mit yndlingsdyr på gården' is clearer but 25 chars.
comb vs bed: Danish uses 'rede' for both hair and bed; comb uses 'kæmme' so the self sheet does not repeat a verb. boots uses 'tage … på', dress uses 'klæde mig på': distinct verbs.
draw: 'Jeg kan farve inden for stregen' is 31 chars (over the 30 target, under the 34 hard max); no shorter natural Danish phrasing keeps the skill.
bake: dropped 'en kage' to stay short; 'hjælpe med at bage' keeps the adult-chef picture honest (the child helps).
kite: the Danish idiom is 'sætte en drage op', not 'flyve med'. umbrella: 'slå en paraply op' is the natural verb.

skip (SHIPPED da 'Jeg kan hoppe'): the EN panel changed this to 'jump rope' and the picture is a girl with a skipping rope. 'Jeg kan hoppe' is a yes for every child and does not name the picture. Recommend updating the shipped da string to 'Jeg kan sjippe' (14 chars), the exact Danish word.

'fiskeri' = the commercial fishing industry; the hobby is 'lystfiskeri', and a child would write 'fiske'.

otherNotes: Headings: all ≤22 chars (longest 'Mit yndlingsinstrument' 22, longest word 19). Gender checked: 'min' + common (frugt, grøntsag, hobby, guf, fugl, morgenmad, form); 'mit' + neuter (kæledyr, instrument, smådyr, havdyr, køretøj, tøj, husdyr).
All 'can' sentences follow the shipped 'Jeg kan …' pattern, first person, no digits, no '{'; all ≤30 chars except 'draw' (31).
washhands follows the shipped 'Jeg kan børste tænder' (no possessive) → 'Jeg kan vaske hænder'.
backpack: 'skoletaske' is what a børnehaveklasse child carries; the picture reads as a school bag.
activities/baking cue shows an adult chef; agree with the EN panel that a child or kitchen-object cue would be better.
Play sheet verbs: synge / tromme / spille (guitar) / bygge / spille (brætspil) / hjælpe med at bage / tage / sætte op: 'spille' twice, as in EN.
